title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E01 — Reflections On and of Pompeii
When most people hear the name of the archeological site of Pompeii, they think of destruction; gaining an overview of the course; considering why the remains of Pompeii offer more than just a story of a cataclysm.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E02 — Geology and Geography On the Bay of Naples
Land and humankind help to shape Pompeii; examining the violent geological forces that forge the distinctive region of the Bay of Naples; tracing its influence on the surrounding geography; the various cultures that contribute to life in this area.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E03 — The Rediscovery of Vesuvian Lands
Archeological finds from the area are unearthed starting around 1594; uncovering the history of Pompeii's excavation in the 1700s, from the kings who plunder its artwork to the modern scholars who seek another kind of treasure.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E04 — Etruscan Pompeii - 5th Century B.C.
While the last days of Pompeii attract popular attention, the city is a thriving cultural center centuries before its destruction; delving deep into Pompeii's remote Etruscan history; exploring what life is like in this ancient pre-Roman settlement.

title: Pompeii: Daily Life in An Ancient Roman City
description:
S01 E05 — Samnite Pompeii - 2nd Century B.C.
Centuries after the establishment of Etruscan Pompeii, the city is invaded by the Samnites; witnessing the conquest of the city by these invaders; considering how Pompeii is redefined and expanded by its new inhabitants.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Point Zéro: Charting Our Course
Contemplating the French art de vivre and the appeal that makes France one of the most visited tourist spots; an overview of the upcoming journey across the rich cultural landscape of France; learning about the iconic figure of Charles de Gaulle.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — The Birth and Rise of Paris
Learning how Paris evolves from an ancient settlement to a Roman city and then the capital; studying medieval Paris through the Cluny Museum, the great cathedral of Notre Dame and the royal chapel of Sainte-Chapelle; following the growth of Paris.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E03 — The Splendor of Versailles
Discovering the Palace of Versailles as the world of Louis XIV; noting how the landscaping surrounding the palace symbolizes features of Louis's reign and how the Versailles court prizes royal spectacle; exploring Louis's patronage of the arts.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E04 — Paris in Revolution
Examining the social and political background of the French Revolution of 1789; visiting key locations in Paris where the events unfold, from a coffee house to the site of the Bastille prison and the Place de la Concorde; mapping Napoleon's rise.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E05 — Northeast to Champagne
Learning about Rheims and the fortunes of its historic and glorious cathedral; studying the beverage that gives this region its name; discovering the area's great champagne makers; visiting the cemeteries and memorials that commemorate World War I.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E01 — Touring the Cradle of Western Civilization
The dynamic civilizations that emerge in the Aegean; the scope of the human drama that is played out there; some of the towering figures and remarkable sites to encounter; Professor Hale's recommendations for traveling this world as the ancients did.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E02 — Athens - Around the Acropolis and Parthenon
The Acropolis is a symbol of Athens; the path of the ancient annual procession honoring Athena; the history and meanings of the site's iconic buildings; the superlative architectural features of the Parthenon and its surprising original uses.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E03 — In the Footsteps of Socrates - Historic Athens
Treasures surrounding the Acropolis; the Theater of Dionysos, where one ponders the rituals of early dramatic festivals; the Odeon of Herodes Atticus, a venue of music and recitations; the Pnyx, an ancient hilltop assembly point; the agora market.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E04 — Around Attica - Temples and Mysteries
Visiting sacred monuments of Greece's beautiful Attica region; the Amphiareion is a shrine of a prophet deity; ancient oracle and healing practices; imposing shrines to Artemis and Poseidon; Eleusis is the site of mystical religious rituals.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E05 — Seeking the Good Life - Corinth to Epidauros
Peloponnese is Greece's southern half; Greece's important sanctuary to Poseidon, where ancient athletes compete to honor the god; Corinth's acropolis and agora; the great healing center of Epidaurus; the best-preserved theater of the ancient world.

title: The Great Tours: Greece and Turkey, From Athens to Istanbul
description:
S01 E06 — Mycenae - Where Kings Planned the Trojan War
The citadel of Mycenae is made famous in Homer's "Iliad"; the imposing Lion Gate; the rulers of Mycenae and ancient life in the citadel; key monuments; the extraordinary shaft graves of an early dynasty; the Megaron palace; the tomb of King Atreus.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E01 — The Norman Conquest Through History
What makes 1066 a pivotal year in the history of Western civilization; how the meaning of the Norman Conquest is debated and interpreted over time; how two weddings lay the groundwork for this moment; information for grasping the Norman Conquest.

title: 1066: The Year That Changed Everything
description:
S01 E02 — England and Normandy Before the Conquest
A closer look at the chaotic half-century between 1016 and 1066; two figures are crucial during this time; Edward the Confessor, who succeeds to the English throne in 1042; William the Bastard, who brings the Norman nobles under control.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E01 — A Tale of Two Ancient Cities
Jericho and Anau are two of the world's oldest cities; their stories have much to say about the scope of human history; what makes these cities successful; how they differ from each other; introducing the concept and key themes of Big History.

title: The Big History of Civilizations
description:
S01 E02 — The Rise of Humanity
Tracing the origins of the human species from the emergence of proto-humans to the rise of Homo sapiens, Professor Benjamin offers perspectives to show what makes the human species unique and why it has been able to flourish.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E01 — Hitler and the Nazi Youth
The horrors of Nazi Germany are one hallmark of World War II; pondering how ordinary German citizens find themselves participating in such heinous events; going inside the propaganda machine of Hitler's Germany; seeing how it targets the youth.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E02 — Japanese Soldiers in Nanjing
The origins of World War II lie in Asia in 1931; tracing the invasion of 1937 and the Rape of Nanjing; witnessing the events through the eyes of a Chinese soldier and a Japanese journalist, young men who bear witness to the flesh and blood of battle.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E01 — Point Zéro: Charting Our Course
Contemplating the French art de vivre and the appeal that makes France one of the most visited tourist spots; an overview of the upcoming journey across the rich cultural landscape of France; learning about the iconic figure of Charles de Gaulle.

title: The Great Tours: France Through the Ages
description:
S01 E02 — The Birth and Rise of Paris
Learning how Paris evolves from an ancient settlement to a Roman city and then the capital; studying medieval Paris through the Cluny Museum, the great cathedral of Notre Dame and the royal chapel of Sainte-Chapelle; following the growth of Paris.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E01 — Ground Rules: Baseball Before Babe Ruth
Why the year 1920 is considered a pivotal year in baseball; achieving a sense of uniformity in the game; examining the years before 1920, when changes in the game were rapid, dramatic, and often surprising.

title: Play Ball! The Rise of Baseball as America's Pastime
description:
S01 E02 — Early Bat and Ball Games
A look back at the beginnings of baseball; how and why the early version of the game evolved in the middle of the 19th century C.E.; learning how early clubs like the Gothams and the Knickerbockers helped repurpose a child's game for urban adults.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Alexander the Great - Conqueror or Tyrant?
Pondering Alexander's identity and story; learning about the ancient sources that contribute to people's understanding of Alexander's life and legacy; examining the ways this figure is perceived by modern scholars.

title: Alexander the Great and the Macedonian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Greece in the Age of Hegemonies
The story of Alexander starts centuries before his birth, in the Greek city-states throughout the Aegean; the conflicts and political crises that shape the Greek world in the generations before Alexander; his father Philip's conquest of the region.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E01 — Native America: A Story of Survival
The commonly held views of Native Americans and the realities of a tapestry of vibrant cultures; Cobb explains the pitfalls that occur when history does not provide this crucial viewpoint; the mistake of consigning Native Americans to the past.

title: Native Peoples of North America
description:
S01 E02 — The Columbian Exchange: New Worlds for All
The misleading dichotomy of Old World and New World impacts perceptions of Native Americans; the Columbian Exchange is the crux behind the creation of new worlds for all; shaping everything from the fauna and flora to the cuisines of the world.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E01 — The Christian Conquest of Rome
An overview of Christianity, the role of Jesus's earliest followers, and a few theories to explain how it became the most widely practiced religion in the world.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E02 — Pagan Religions in the Roman World
Insight into the significance of paganism, a complex term used in the pre-Christian Roman Empire to refer to the polytheistic religions that were widely followed at the time.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E03 — Judaism in the Roman World
Insight into the significance of Judaism, an ancient monotheistic religion that was initially practiced by many, including Jesus and his early followers.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Christianity in the Roam World: An Overview
Christianity's success stems from its similarities to and differences from other religious practices.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E05 — The Life and Teachings ofJesus
Historians, Gospels, and other sources of information provide insight into Jesus's life and the teachings that led to the beginning of Christianity.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E06 — The Beginning of Christianity
Insight into how Jesus's sacrifice led to the birth of Christianity and had an everlasting impact on the lives of the disciples who had lost all hope at the time.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E05 — The Beginnings of the Gospel Traditions
This lecture looks at the roots of the Gospel narratives in the oral traditions that are spread throughout the Mediterranean in the years after Jesus' death; how they might be modified; what one can know about their historical accuracy.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E01 — A Quartet of Sages
The legacies of Confucius, the Buddha, Jesus and Muhammad (PBUH); the lenses of metaphysics, philosophical anthropology, ethics and spiritual practice for assessing their contribution; comparing the vision and wisdom of these extraordinary sages.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E02 — Confucius's China
The nature of Chinese identity in Confucius's time as cultural rather than political; the Chinese orientation to the past; an earlier era of moral kingship; social and political upheavals in the Zhou dynasty; the stage for Confucius's teaching.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E03 — Becoming a Sage
Reconstructing the life of Confucius, centering on the famous Analects, a compendium of conversations and sayings; the known facts of his lineage; the unusual circumstances of his birth; his poverty-stricken childhood; his great love of learning.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E04 — A Gentleman and a Scholar
Confucius's journey reveals the actions that underlay his teaching; the qualities of humility, empathy and love of virtue that inform his life as a state official; his period of self-imposed exile; his final years of teaching and introspection.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E05 — Heaven and Earth
Confucian metaphysics stands on the foundation of the ancient Chinese view of ultimate reality; Zhou dynasty cosmology; its conception of Tian (Heaven) and Di (Earth); the hierarchy of divine beings; Confucius's non-theocentric view of Heaven.

Insight into the significance of Judaism, an ancient monotheistic religion that was initially practiced by many, including Jesus and his early followers.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E04 — Christianity in the Roam World: An Overview
Christianity's success stems from its similarities to and differences from other religious practices.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E05 — The Life and Teachings ofJesus
Historians, Gospels, and other sources of information provide insight into Jesus's life and the teachings that led to the beginning of Christianity.

title: The Triumph of Christianity
description:
S01 E06 — The Beginning of Christianity
Insight into how Jesus's sacrifice led to the birth of Christianity and had an everlasting impact on the lives of the disciples who had lost all hope at the time.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E01 — The New Testament-An Overview
The course begins by addressing some of the basic facts about the New Testament; which books it contains, when they are written, in what language and by whom.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E02 — Paul-Our Earliest Christian Author
The Epistles of Paul are the earliest books of the New Testament, predating even the Gospels; the realities of writing a letter in the ancient world; issues that affect how one understands Paul's Epistles and the other writings of the New Testament.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E03 — The Pauline Epistles
This lecture looks at some of the major teachings of Paul's Epistles; showing how he shapes his theological and ethical views in light of the problems that emerge in his burgeoning Christian communities.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E04 — The Problem of Pseudonymity
This lecture considers the broad problem of pseudonymity, or forgery, in the ancient world; applying one's findings to the Pauline letters of the New Testament to see if any, in fact, are written by Paul's followers rather than Paul himself.

title: The History of the Bible: The Making of the New Testament Canon
description:
S01 E05 — The Beginnings of the Gospel Traditions
This lecture looks at the roots of the Gospel narratives in the oral traditions that are spread throughout the Mediterranean in the years after Jesus' death; how they might be modified; what one can know about their historical accuracy.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E01 — A Quartet of Sages
The legacies of Confucius, the Buddha, Jesus and Muhammad (PBUH); the lenses of metaphysics, philosophical anthropology, ethics and spiritual practice for assessing their contribution; comparing the vision and wisdom of these extraordinary sages.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E02 — Confucius's China
The nature of Chinese identity in Confucius's time as cultural rather than political; the Chinese orientation to the past; an earlier era of moral kingship; social and political upheavals in the Zhou dynasty; the stage for Confucius's teaching.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E03 — Becoming a Sage
Reconstructing the life of Confucius, centering on the famous Analects, a compendium of conversations and sayings; the known facts of his lineage; the unusual circumstances of his birth; his poverty-stricken childhood; his great love of learning.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E04 — A Gentleman and a Scholar
Confucius's journey reveals the actions that underlay his teaching; the qualities of humility, empathy and love of virtue that inform his life as a state official; his period of self-imposed exile; his final years of teaching and introspection.

title: Confucius, Buddha, Jesus, and Muhammad
description:
S01 E05 — Heaven and Earth
Confucian metaphysics stands on the foundation of the ancient Chinese view of ultimate reality; Zhou dynasty cosmology; its conception of Tian (Heaven) and Di (Earth); the hierarchy of divine beings; Confucius's non-theocentric view of Heaven.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E01 — Hunting, Gathering, and Stone Age Cooking
Food as a major catalyst in human history; what food choices reveal about one's values and ambitions; studying food culture in prehistoric times; a wide-ranging diet; the ways in which how human ancestors ate directly drove evolution.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E02 — What Early Agriculturalists Ate
The transition to agriculture; exploring the factors surrounding the rise of agriculture; how plants and animals were domesticated; why agriculture directly led to civilization; how the menu of foods favored by agricultural societies came about.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E03 — Egypt and the Gift of the Nile
Ancient Egypt's prosperity and advantages; a sophisticated food tradition and the first elite cuisine; the archeological evidence of Egypt's food customs; the religious significance of foodstuffs and animals; the components of Egyptian cuisine.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E04 — Ancient Judea - From Eden to Kosher Laws
Why practices regarding food were integral to the lives of the ancient Hebrews; exploring prescriptions regarding food in Genesis; considering that the Fall was an act of eating; Hebrew rituals and the meaning of sacrifice; complex food prohibitions.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E05 — Classical Greece - Wine, Olive Oil, and Trade
How the ancient Greeks' need for arable land led to their imperial and mercantile systems; what can be learned about ancient Greek food culture; the role of food in rituals; classical Greek diet components that later influenced the rest of the world.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E06 — The Alexandrian Exchange and the Four Humors
Alexander's conquests herald an era where previously unconnected cultures mix; tracing the diffusion of foodstuffs over trade networks in the Hellenistic period; studying early dietary regimens based on Galen's famous theory of the body's humors.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E07 — Ancient India - Sacred Cows and Ayurveda
Ancient India's culinary traditions carry a wide influence; learning about the culture of the Aryans, whose religion prefigures Hinduism; food customs relating to caste and the traditions of vegetarianism in Hinduism, Jainism, and Buddhism.

title: Food: A Cultural Culinary History
description:
S01 E08 — Yin and Yang of Classical Chinese Cuisine
Chinese culture produces what is arguably the most complex and varied culinary tradition on Earth; tracing the rise of civilization in China from the Hsia to the Han dynasty; the social and technological factors underlying China's food traditions.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E01 — Japan: A Globally Engaged Island Nation
Japanese culture is shaped by powerful cycles of globalization and isolation; the earliest human habitation of Japan; the origins of its rich culture; the perfect starting points for dispelling common Western misconceptions about this island nation.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E02 — Understanding Japan Through Ancient Myths
An introduction to ancient Japanese myths, collectively known as Shinto; the oldest written compilation of Japanese oral tradition, the Kojiki; stories about gods and heroes; the origins of the universe, the Rock Cave of Heaven and rival clans.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E03 — The Emergence of the Ritsuryo State
In the late 500s, Japan begins a project of state building that evolves into the emperor-led Ritsuryo state; the state's laws and accomplishments; how this political centralization is inspired by the emergence of powerful states in China and Korea.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E04 — Aspects of the Japanese Language
A complex writing system; how spoken Japanese reflects a long-standing concern with order, hierarchy and consensus; social context is important when speaking Japanese; the linguistic consequences of adopting Chinese characters in Japanese writing.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E05 — Early Japanese Buddhism
Professor Ravina explains why Buddhism is so appealing in ancient Japan; three key observations about the religion's earliest form; the two main strands of Japanese Buddhism; the more esoteric tradition of Shingon; the more accessible Pure Land.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E06 — Heian Court Culture
Japan's first period of isolation; the rise of the Heian court, ancient Japan's cultured and exclusive aristocracy; the powerful Fujiwara family; how the novel "The Tale of Genji" reveals the court's penchant for scandal and intrigue.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E07 — The Rise of the Samurai
From the court in Kyoto to the countryside, where political infighting leads to the rise of Japan's first shogunate; the emergence of the samurai; the rise of warrior culture through the lines of "The Tale of the Heike", an epic ballad.

title: Understanding Japan: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E08 — Pure Land Buddhism and Zen Buddhism
The decline of the court and the rise of the warrior class shape the evolution of Buddhist aesthetic, spiritual and philosophical concepts; the massive growth of Pure Land Buddhism, the dominant form in Japan today; the main schools of Zen Buddhism.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E01 — Europe on the Brink of the Black Death
Contemplating the enormity of the Black Death's impact on the medieval world; taking account of the state of medieval society on the eve of the plague; investigating the religious, economic, and political structures of mid-14th-century Europe.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E02 — The Epidemiology of Plague
Exploring the medical understanding of the plague; the sixth-century Plague of Justinian; the Black Death of the 1300s; the 19th-century Third Pandemic; examining the three predominant varieties of plague and their symptomatologies.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E03 — Did Plague Really Cause the Black Death?
Reassessing the causes of the Black Death; questioning how it spread through medieval Europe with astonishing speed and virulence; investigating additional factors that may have contributed to the devastation, such as other diseases and bacteria.

title: The Black Death: The World's Most Devastating Plague
description:
S01 E04 — The Black Death's Ports of Entry
Examining the plague's first sustained appearance in Europe; the Mongol siege that preceded the outbreak; how the plague moved west with escaping sailors; following the spread of the plague to Constantinople, Italy, France and England.
